title: Portfolio Listings
text:
How It Works

Create a folder for your items, such as portfolio/.
Add one .qmd file per project with a title, date, description, image, and categories.
Add a listing: block to the page that should display them.
Place a div with the listing’s id where the listing should appear.


Step 2: One project file


portfolio/rkr-newsletter.qmd

---
title: "RKR Newsletter A/B Testing"
description: "Testing newsletter design to grow restaurant reservations."
date: 2026-10-05
image: rkr.png
categories: [Analytics, A/B Testing, Culminating Project]
---



Step 3: The listing block on this page


listings.qmd

listing:
  - id: portfolio-grid
    contents: portfolio        # which folder to gather
    type: grid                 # default, grid, or table
    sort: "date desc"          # newest first
    categories: true           # clickable category filter
    fields: [image, title, description, categories, date]



Step 4: Where it appears
::: {#portfolio-grid}
:::

title: Portfolio Listings
text:
Useful Listing Options

contents: a folder, a list of files, or a pattern like "portfolio/*.qmd".
sort: order items by date, title, or any field, ascending or descending.
categories: show a clickable category list built from each item’s tags.
filter-ui and sort-ui: add a search box and sort menu for visitors.
page-size: split long listings into pages.
feed: true: create an RSS feed so followers get your new posts.







TipWhy this matters for a portfolio



Recruiters skim. A listing gives them a clean, filterable overview, and the categories show the range of your skills at a glance.

title: RKR Newsletter Dashboard
text:
How the Test Works
The project runs in two phases during the 2026 to 2027 school year:

Fall: button placement. Move the “Reserve a Table” button to the upper left of RKR’s section and compare against past issues.
Spring: image vs. video. Keep the button fixed and split each issue so half of readers see an image and half see a video.

title: RKR Newsletter Dashboard
section: What You Can Do in the Dashboard
text:
What You Can Do in the Dashboard

OverviewFall TestSpring TestData


Headline numbers for every tracked issue: open rate, “Reserve a Table” click rate, and OpenTable reservations, plus a week by week trend.


Compares the upper-left button against the baseline, with a two-proportion test to check whether the lift is more than chance.


Compares image and video formats side by side using the same click and reservation measures.


A searchable, sortable table of every issue so you can check any number yourself.

title: RKR Newsletter Dashboard
text:
Key Measures








Measure
How it is calculated
Why it matters




Open rate
Opens ÷ recipients
Shows whether readers see the newsletter at all


Reserve click rate
“Reserve a Table” clicks ÷ opens
Shows whether RKR’s section earns attention


Reservations
OpenTable bookings attributed to the newsletter
The business outcome RKR cares about









NoteAbout the data



Real issue data is still being collected. The dashboard currently runs on an illustrative sample (data/rkr_newsletter.csv) built to match the test design. Swapping in real data only requires replacing that one CSV file; every chart and statistic updates on the next render.

title: Styling a Quarto Website with CSS and SCSS
section: CSS vs. SCSS: What’s the Difference?
text:
CSS vs. SCSS: What’s the Difference?



CSS (Cascading Style Sheets)

The language browsers read to style a page
Every color and size is written out by hand
Great for small, one-off tweaks






SCSS (Sassy CSS)

A more powerful version that compiles into CSS
Adds variables, nesting, mixins, and color math
What Quarto themes are built on

title: Styling a Quarto Website with CSS and SCSS
text:
How Quarto Applies Your Styles

Create a style file in your project folder, such as custom.scss.
Point _quarto.yml to it under format: html: theme:.
Render the site. Quarto compiles the SCSS with the Bootstrap theme and applies it to every page.



_quarto.yml

format:
  html:
    theme:
      light: [cosmo, custom.scss]   # base theme first, your file second

Listing custom.scss after cosmo means your choices override the theme’s defaults.






TipPlain CSS works too



For a simple .css file, use css: styles.css instead of adding it to theme. You lose SCSS features but it is quick for small changes.

section: Tips for Styling Your Own Site
text:
Tips for Styling Your Own Site

Start with a theme: pick a Bootswatch theme like cosmo or flatly, then customize only what you need.
Set variables first: changing $primary does more than dozens of manual rules.
Inspect the page: right click any element and choose Inspect to find the class name you want to style.
Re-render after edits: run quarto render so the new styles reach the docs folder before you push.







NoteLearn more



The Quarto HTML Theming guide lists every variable you can change.
